info.title: Engineers Notebook store
info.description:
The store keeps teams' documents in workspaces and decides who may open and change each one.

**Access.** Every `/v2` route resolves the caller from their session, then checks their role in the workspace concerned: `viewer`, `editor` or `owner`, the highest of their individual role, the role of any identity-provider group of theirs the workspace maps, and `owner` for a store administrator. Each operation names the least role it needs in `x-required-role`. Someone with no role in a workspace gets 404 for it and everything in it, the same as for one that does not exist; someone whose role is too low gets 403.

**Sessions.** Sign in by sending the browser to `/v1/auth/{provider}/start`. The store sets an HttpOnly cookie, `sd_session`, which every other call carries. Sessions last eight hours.

**Writes.** A request that changes something must have no `Origin` header, or one that is the store's own origin or in `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` (else 403 `forbidden-origin`), and a body, if any, of `application/json` (else 415).

**Replies.** Errors are `{ error: { reason, message } }`. A reply about a document carries `X-Document-Version`. Nothing is cacheable: every reply carries `Cache-Control: no-store`.

**Documents** are stored as the editor sends them. The server and its administrators can read them.

200.description: Up.

relayAuthentication.description: `required` when the relay only admits people carrying a token from this store (`RELAY_TOKEN_SECRET`).

200.description: Provider ids, each usable in `/v1/auth/{provider}/start`.

302.description: Sends the browser to the identity provider.

get.description: A browser navigation, not an API call. After the provider returns the browser to `/v1/auth/callback`, the store sets the session cookie and redirects to `returnTo`, or to `AFTER_LOGIN_URL` when none was given.

parameters.name: returnTo
parameters.description: The page to come back to. Its origin must be the store's own or one in `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`; any other is refused with 400 before the sign-in starts.

get.summary: Where the identity provider returns the browser

302.description: Signed in. Sets the session cookie and redirects to the editor.

get.description: Not called directly. `state` is single use and expires after ten minutes.

200.description: The session.

groupsOverage.description: The provider had more groups for this person than it would send, so roles from groups may be missing.

204.description: The session is ended and the cookie cleared. Succeeds whether or not anyone was signed in.

post.summary: A relay token for a session started by link

200.description: A token admitting the caller to that room on the relay for ten minutes.

post.description: For sessions people start themselves and share by link. Refused with 403 for a workspace document's room (`wsdoc-…`), whose token comes from `/v2/documents/{docId}/session`. Answers 404 where the relay does not require tokens.

get.summary: What kind of store this is

200.description: A store that serves workspaces. An older store answers 404 here.

mode.description: The server keeps documents as sent and can read them.

get.summary: The caller, and what they may do store-wide

200.description: The caller.
Workspaces the caller has a role in, by name.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Include archived workspaces. Only takes effect for a store administrator.

post.x-required-role: administrator, or anyone signed in where WORKSPACE_CREATION=anyone

201.description: The workspace, with the caller's role in it.

post.description: The caller becomes its first owner. Names are unique, ignoring case.

200.description: The workspace, with the caller's role in it.
The workspace, with the caller's role in it.
The workspace, with the caller's role in it.

post.description: Its members no longer see it or its documents. Nothing is deleted, and nothing in it can be changed until it is restored.

200.description: The workspace, with the caller's role in it.
People added by name, and identity-provider groups given a role.

put.summary: Add someone, or change their role

200.description: The member.

put.description: The person must have signed in to the store at least once.

200.description: Removed.

delete.description: A role they have through a group is unaffected.

put.summary: Give a group a role, or change it

200.description: The mapping.

put.description: Everyone in the group has the role from their next sign-in. The group is named in the body, never the path: a name may contain a slash (Keycloak's full paths start with one), which a proxy serving the store under a prefix would rewrite.

group.description: Exactly as it appears in the groups claim.

200.description: Removed.

get.summary: Find people to add, by name

200.description: Up to twenty people who have signed in to the store and whose name contains the query.
In the order they were added.

parameters.name: deleted
parameters.description: Include deleted documents still being kept.

post.description: Its content follows as updates. The id is chosen by the caller and must be unique in the store; `local` is refused, because it is the id every browser gives its own first document.

200.description: The document and its whole update log.

patch.summary: Retitle a document, or move it to another workspace
patch.x-required-role: editor; to move, editor in both workspaces

200.description: The document.
The document, now deleted. It is kept for the store's retention period and can be restored.
The document.
Updates with a version greater than `since`.

post.description: An update is a Yjs update, base64-encoded. The store keeps it as sent and does not parse it.

expectedVersion.description: Refused with 409 if the document is no longer at this version.

post.summary: Replace the update log with one snapshot

200.description: Compacted.

post.description: Send `expectedVersion`: without it, a snapshot made a moment ago would erase an update someone else appended since.

200.description: The same room and key for everyone who may edit the document.

key.description: Encrypts what passes through the relay between browsers.

relayToken.description: For that room and this caller, valid ten minutes. Null where the relay does not require tokens.

get.description: A peer in a session can send changes to the others directly, so being able to read the document is not enough: viewers are refused, and follow through `/updates` instead.

200.description: The document.

put.description: Keeps the document from being removed, by retention or by an administrator, until released.

200.description: The document.

post.summary: Remove a deleted document for good

200.description: Gone. This cannot be undone.

post.description: Refused with 409 while the document is under hold, or not deleted.

IfDocumentVersion.name: If-Document-Version
IfDocumentVersion.description: The highest version of this document the caller has seen. A store that would answer with an older one refuses with 409 `stale-version` instead, which is how a rolled-back store is noticed.

DocumentVersion.description: The document's version after this request.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed; the message says how.

Unauthenticated.description: Not signed in, or the session has expired.

Forbidden.description: Signed in, but the caller's role does not allow this, the action is for administrators, or the request did not come from the editor.

NotFound.description: No such thing, or one the caller has no role in. The two are not told apart.

Conflict.description: Refused because of the current state: a name or id already taken, a version that has moved on, a document under hold.

Deleted.description: The document is deleted. Restore it first.

TooLarge.description: The body or the update exceeds the store's limits.

reason.description: Stable, for a client to branch on: `unauthenticated`, `forbidden`, `forbidden-origin`, `not-found`, `conflict`, `stale-version`, `deleted`, `bad-request`, `too-large`, `quota`, `unsupported`, `internal`.

Role.description: `viewer` opens documents. `editor` also creates, changes, deletes and restores them. `owner` also renames the workspace and manages its members and groups.

via.description: How the caller came by that role.

groups.description: As the identity provider reported them at sign-in.

version.description: Increases on every accepted write, and on delete and restore.

purgeAfter.description: When a deleted document will be removed. Null while it is not deleted, under indefinite retention, or under hold.

DocumentWrite.description: Where the document stands after a write to its log.
